edges.description: Riboflavin is the only precursor of FMN and FAD, which are formed inside cells.
Glutathione reductase is an FAD-dependent enzyme whose holoenzyme fraction falls when FAD is scarce.
Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is generated by an FMN-dependent oxidase.
Riboflavin, as FAD, is the cofactor of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase.
Succinate dehydrogenase (complex II) and other flavoproteins of the citric acid cycle and respiratory chain need FAD or FMN.
Poor riboflavin status impairs iron absorption and mobilization of iron from stores; the flavoproteins responsible have not been established.
Riboflavin is needed to maintain skin and mucous membranes; which flavoproteins fail in the epithelium is not established.
Corneal vascularization is a rare sign of dietary riboflavin deficiency; the mechanism is not established.
Undersaturated enzyme gives low basal activity and a raised activation coefficient.
Loss of flavin-dependent antioxidant capacity is followed by oxidative stress in animal models; the contribution of glutathione reductase specifically has not been isolated.
Less PLP is formed, so plasma PLP falls as riboflavin status worsens.
Reduced MTHFR flux limits homocysteine remethylation.
In MTHFR 677TT homozygotes, raising riboflavin status lowers systolic blood pressure; the link between one-carbon metabolism and blood pressure is not established.
Reduced energy production is proposed to cause fatigue.
Limited iron supply and flavin depletion reduce red cell production.
Reduced erythroid production lowers hemoglobin.
In severe deficiency the marrow erythroid compartment is hypoplastic.
Inflammation and fissuring at the oral commissures.
Inflammation of the lips (cheilosis).
Inflamed, magenta-coloured tongue.
Greasy scaling dermatitis, typically perinasal and perioral.
Inflammatory dermatitis of the scrotal skin.
Low intake is the principal route to systemic riboflavin depletion.
Alcohol impairs intestinal riboflavin uptake and renal conservation.

edges.limitations: The abstract does not describe which signs constituted ariboflavinosis in the rats, and the esophageal atrophy has no established human counterpart.
Retinal dysfunction has not been documented in human nutritional ariboflavinosis, and the degree of depletion exceeds most human dietary exposure.
Genetic transporter loss, closer to SLC52A3 riboflavin transporter deficiency than to dietary deficiency, and more severe than typical human nutritional depletion.
Diagnosis was ex juvantibus from feed analysis and response to a B-complex supplement; the reproductive phenotype has no documented counterpart in human nutritional deficiency.

nodes.description: Angular stomatitis, with erythema and fissuring at the corners of the mouth. Its cause is not specific to riboflavin: in Indian schoolboys it did not respond to B-complex supplementation but did respond to topical antiseptic, suggesting infection contributes.

The glutathione reductase apoenzyme in red cells is incompletely saturated with FAD, so basal activity is low and rises when FAD is added in vitro. The ratio of stimulated to basal activity (EGRAC) is the functional biomarker of riboflavin status. Activity is restored by riboflavin in vivo, which separates this acquired state from hereditary glutathione reductase deficiency.
